neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. Anxious but cooperative. Speech fluent and normal.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. Extraocular movements full, pupils equal and reactive. No facial weakness, no ptosis. Bulbar function intact — normal speech and swallowing.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric flaccid weakness, legs more than arms. Hip flexion 3/5 bilaterally, knee flexion/extension 4-/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Shoulder abduction 4/5, grip strength 4-/5 bilaterally. Tone reduced throughout. No fasciculations. Unable to rise from a chair without using the arms.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild distal paresthesias in the feet and fingertips. Light touch and pinprick mildly reduced in a stocking distribution; vibration mildly reduced at the toes. No sensory level.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Global areflexia — biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, knee, and ankle jerks all absent bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact in the arms; leg testing limited by weakness, with no cerebellar signs.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to walk unassisted — requires support, with a steppage pattern from bilateral foot drop. Romberg deferred due to weakness.
neurological_exam.additional: Bedside spirometry: forced vital capacity (FVC) 2.6 L (~70% predicted), single-breath count 28 — adequate but warrants serial monitoring. Community-acquired pneumonia 3 weeks ago, fully resolved. Received a seasonal influenza vaccine 4 days ago. No fever at presentation. No trauma, no toxic ingestion, no tick exposure, and no recent travel.

patient.chief_complaint: One-week history of progressive, symmetric ascending limb weakness with global areflexia, preceded by pneumonia three weeks earlier.
patient.history_present_illness: A 19-year-old woman presents with one week of progressive limb weakness. Symptoms began with tingling in both feet and difficulty climbing stairs, and over seven days ascended to involve the thighs and then the hands, with mild distal numbness. She now cannot walk without assistance and struggles to rise from a chair. Three weeks ago she had community-acquired pneumonia, treated with a course of oral antibiotics and now fully resolved. Four days ago she received a seasonal influenza vaccine at a campus clinic. She reports no fever, no bladder or bowel dysfunction, no back pain, no diplopia, and no difficulty breathing or swallowing. There is no history of trauma, toxic ingestion, tick exposure, or recent travel. Her maternal grandmother has multiple sclerosis, but there is no family history of hereditary neuropathy. On examination she has symmetric flaccid weakness that is greater in the legs than the arms, mild distal sensory loss in a stocking-glove pattern, and global areflexia — absent reflexes in all four limbs are the critical finding pointing to an acute polyradiculoneuropathy rather than a myelopathy or a functional cause.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (classic AIDP)

differential.key_features: Sensory level / sphincter dysfunction absent; spinal MRI excludes.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Start continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry for the period of maximal weakness and keep it running alongside serial respiratory function. Autonomic instability affects about two thirds of patients and is a leading cause of in-hospital death: bradyarrhythmias, pauses beyond 3 seconds and blood-pressure lability are what trigger ICU escalation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus rhythm with intermittent mild sinus tachycardia; no malignant arrhythmia and no significant bradycardia — the recording is read for the bradyarrhythmias, pauses beyond 3 seconds and blood-pressure lability that trigger ICU escalation

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

contraindicated_actions: Do not start corticosteroids as monotherapy.
key_reasoning_points: Brighton level 1 case: classic AIDP with all supportive features.
